The 90-minute launch window opens at 5:30 p.m. CT, with SpaceX live coverage beginning around 30 minutes before liftoff.

Weather conditions are currently 85% favorable for flight as Starbase prepares for another historic test mission.

SpaceX just Starship Version 3 — and nearly every major system has been redesigned.

Major upgrades include:

• Payload capacity increased to 100 metric tons
• All 33 Raptor engines now ignite simultaneously
• Grid fins reduced from 4 to 3, but each is 50% larger
• Hot-stage adapter is now fully reusable
• Engine shielding has been removed
• Massive new internal fuel transfer tube roughly the size of a Falcon 9 first stage
• Up to 60 Starlink V3 satellites per launch
• New docking ports designed for in-orbit refueling missions

One of the wildest details is the redesigned fuel transfer system.

The internal transfer tube is so enormous that SpaceX engineers described it as “basically putting a rocket inside a rocket.”
